text.p: Broker Salomon Brothers reiterated its buy recommendation for Istituto Mobiliare Italiano (IMI), saying the investment banking group remains its preferred investment in the Italian banking sector.
It added in a research note that it based this recommendation on the basis of the group's very solid balance sheet, superior earnings record and relative valuation.

It pointed out that the benefits of IMI's restructuring at home and selected rationalisation abroad should shine through in 1996 in a four-point improvement in the group's cost/income ratio to 36 percent, or a nine point drop since 1994.
Combined with a jump in other income, the lower cost base should lead to a 20 percent rise in 1996 net income before extraordinaries, and a more than 25 percent rise after extraordinaries.
At 1010 GMT, IMI shares were up 0.06 percent at 12,600 lire in a generally lower Milan bourse.
